newsitem.title: USA: TACA Airlines chief sees Latam growth.
newsitem.headline: TACA Airlines chief sees Latam growth.

text.p: Federico Bloch, chief executive of TACA International Airlines SA, predicted big growth of air traffic within Latin America, as carriers like his serve ever- smaller cities.
"There will be tremendous growth in the regional markets in Latin America," Bloch said in a Thursday speech to the Americas Conference on Aviation.

Only 20 percent of Latin American air traffic involves flights to the United States, he said, with 80 percent travel within the region. Since 1990 the region has seen 50 new airlines open for business.
And yet "among cities with populations of more than 50,000, there are 50 city pairs without daily non-stop service. We are seeing just the tip of the iceburg," he said.
Some of these citiy pairs with no daily non-stop service include Bogota-Mexico City, Bogota-Lima and San Jose-Quito.

Some regional carriers are "taking air service to developing communities," he said. The Salvadoran carrier plans to "start the same thing in Costa Rica and we hope to extend this to many Central American countries."

But the biggest constraint to growth in Latin American aviation is infrastructure, he said. "It will take years to plan and construct" the necessary infrastructure and "we already have infrastructure issues today."
